Our distinction between small and large arms is not just for the sake of obtaining a PTAS. In fact, we do not know if there is a completely uncrossed, O(1)-approximate solution. For instance, we have an example where iterating the fractional uncrossing argument to uncross all arms may create a fractional arm whose length is longer than B by a super-constant factor. 3.2 Finding a Well-Formed Solution 3.2.1 Step Min-max Cost Theorem 7 shows that there is a solution of cost at most (1 + 2)B such that no two small arms (i.e. length ≤ B) used to assign clients to centers cross. Call this solution SB0 . We now show that we can find such a well-structured solution of cost at most (1 + 8)B.
